correctness.rationale: The trace pairing is nondegenerate, so Fourier orthogonality converts the fourth norm to weighted additive energy. For every nonzero sum \(s\), the two conic equations for \(a\) and \(s-a\) intersect in at most two points and the existing pair \(a,b\) exhausts that fiber up to swapping; the zero fiber consists of all \(q+1\) ordered antipodal pairs. Hence the package's exact identity \(\mathcal Q=2S^2-P_4-2R+|B_0|^2\) is correct. Grouping antipodal pairs, phase alignment and then equalizing the two moduli within each pair and the pair masses globally gives \(\mathcal Q\le3qS^2/(q+1)\), with equality exactly at constant modulus and common antipodal product phase. Substitution of the normalized \(L^2\) norm yields the stated constant. Independent brute-force reconstruction over prime fields \(q=3,5,7,11,13\) reproduced \(|T|=q+1\), zero-fiber size \(q+1\), nonzero-fiber maximum two, and energy \(3q(q+1)\).

It neither resolves the exceptional zero-sum fiber sharply nor optimizes weighted energy or classifies equality. The 2024 sharp finite-field extension program covers other named surfaces, and Ronda's 2026 sharp theorem is for quadratic surfaces in three dimensions, not planar conics. final_claim: For the anisotropic norm-one conic \(T=\{z\in\mathbb F_{q^2}:N(z)=1\}\) over every odd \(q\), with normalized surface measure and counting measure on the ambient additive plane, the exact sharp fourth-moment extension constant is \(R_T^*(2\to4)^4=3q^3/(q+1)^3\); nonzero extremizers are exactly the constant-modulus functions whose antipodal products have one common argument.
